result.title: Writer-independent handedness identification from offline Bangla handwriting under controlled acquisition
result.summary: Handedness is a soft-biometric cue for forensic document examination and writer profiling, yet reported accuracies from offline handwriting rarely keep writers, texts and image acquisition apart, so models may recognise the writer or capture conditions rather than the writing hand. Such controlled evidence is missing for Bangla. Using our BanglaHand dataset of 42 writers (21 left- and 21 right-handed), who each wrote six shared prompts and two own texts under controlled collection and photography, we evaluate handedness identification with all images of each test writer held out, whole-writer permutation tests and photometric controls. An ink-gradient descriptor identified the handedness of unseen writers with 77.4% balanced accuracy (95% writer-bootstrap interval 67.7-86.5%; p=0.001) and frozen ImageNet embeddings with 69.5-72.0%. Part of this signal is stroke darkness: in a post hoc analysis, right-handed writers' strokes were darker at their centres for equal stroke width, consistent with higher pen pressure and not explained by lighting drift. With ink density and brightness regressed out, the descriptor still reached 64.5% (p=0.027), whereas writing-only shape features were weaker (60.8%; p=0.090). Handedness is thus identifiable from offline Bangla handwriting under controlled acquisition, and photometric controls are essential to interpret such cues.

AI.brief_summary: 基于自建 BanglaHand 数据集，在留一书写者、整书写者置换检验与光度控制下评估离线孟加拉文手写对左右利手的可识别性，发现墨迹梯度描述子可识别未见书写者，且笔画深浅（笔压）是部分信号来源。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文属手写笔迹软生物特征与取证鉴定，涉及的是书写者属性识别与光度混杂控制，与 VLM 的视觉细节表示、latent 推理状态或证据获取、停止决策均无实质关联，也无具体可借鉴线索。
